scenes.headline: How three.js draws a mesh as clusters of 64 triangles
scenes.sub: Compute passes cull and an indirect draw submits the survivors.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tessel! three.js now has a pipeline that cuts meshes into small clusters and lets the graphics card decide which to draw. Here is how it works.

scenes.text: Cut each mesh into clusters of 64 triangles once, then let compute shaders cull clusters and write the draw call themselves.
scenes.say: The idea: cut each mesh into clusters of sixty-four triangles, once. Then compute shaders cull the clusters every frame and write the draw arguments themselves.

steps.say: First, one thread per object tests its bounding sphere against the six frustum planes and picks a level of detail from its projected error.
Next, one thread per cluster. A cone test drops clusters that face away from the camera. A frustum test drops those off screen.
Survivors are appended to a work queue with an atomic counter.
A last thread writes the draw arguments: one hundred ninety-two vertices, and one instance per surviving cluster. The processor never reads the count.

left.title: In this pull request
left.say: It has clusters, GPU culling, and indirect draws. A second pipeline adds a software rasterizer for small triangles and a visibility buffer.

right.title: Not in it
right.say: What it lacks is the virtual part. Level of detail is chosen per object, not per cluster, and all levels stay in memory. Nothing streams.

scenes.label: triangles in the demo at full detail
scenes.say: The demo scene holds eight hundred nineteen million triangles at full detail. That is a ceiling on the scene, not on what is drawn.

scenes.title: Sphere clusters culled by the cone
scenes.note: My CPU reimplementation, not the pipeline's builder.
scenes.say: I rebuilt the clusters on the CPU. On a sphere, the cone test culls less as the camera backs away, and it never culled a visible triangle.

scenes.text: Clusters and indirect draws are real here. Hierarchical level of detail and streaming are what is missing.

scenes.say: Clusters, GPU culling, and indirect draws are in. Cluster level of detail and streaming are not.
